item.text:
Completed a bounded continuation across Chapters 2B–8B. Chapter 1B’s prior continuation (E022–E034) was preserved; no new nuclear unit was promoted.

The workspace remained read-only, so I could not physically update `research-ledger-manifest.json`. The following provisional units should be appended with globally unique IDs E035–E079. Exact existing `methodology_ids` must be copied from the authoritative manifest; I have not invented lens IDs.

### 2B — external security and peace

- **E035** — Storting scrutiny identified that Ukrainian defence donations were governed by executive foreign/security policy rather than ordinary export controls; attribution is cabinet-level, not personal. Contrary oversight requested disclosure of third-country resale controls. [Storting lines 523–551](https://www.stortinget.no/no/Saker-og-publikasjoner/Publikasjoner/Innstillinger/Stortinget/2022-2023/inns-202223-024s/?all=true)
- **E036** — Parliamentary debate recorded broad support for Ukraine donations while acknowledging the decision as an exceptional change in Norwegian policy. [Storting lines 561–562](https://www.stortinget.no/no/Saker-og-publikasjoner/Publikasjoner/Referater/Stortinget/2022-2023/refs-202223-10-20/?all=true)
- **E037** — Opposition MPs alleged that a Russian-vessel port exception could benefit Putin-linked oligarchs and weaken sanctions; this is parliamentary allegation, not an adjudicated finding against Støre. [Storting lines 526–530](https://www.stortinget.no/no/Saker-og-publikasjoner/Publikasjoner/Innstillinger/Stortinget/2022-2023/inns-202223-024s/?all=true)
- **E038** — Government export-control framework required human-rights, humanitarian-law, and recipient-country assessments, but target-year evidence does not establish how each Ukrainian transfer was monitored after delivery. [Government report lines 197–229](https://www.regjeringen.no/globalassets/departementene/ud/dokumenter/rapporter/meldst14_20212022_eng.pdf)
- **E039** — Government reported ongoing assessment of Ukrainian military donations, security-based limits on publication, and continued Storting briefing. This supports formal process but leaves transparency and outcome questions unresolved. [Government report lines 244–277](https://www.regjeringen.no/globalassets/departementene/ud/dokumenter/rapporter/meldst14_20212022_eng.pdf)
- **E040** — Storting later required a government explanation of how Norwegian export rules and binding agreements would apply to re-exported matériel, directly documenting an accountability gap. [Storting lines 545–551](https://www.stortinget.no/no/Saker-og-publikasjoner/Publikasjoner/Innstillinger/Stortinget/2022-2023/inns-202223-024s/?all=true)

Shortfall: no recipient-side civilian-harm assessment, weapon end-use audit, or reliable intelligence-correction record was recovered.

### 3B — protection, rights, and human security

- **E041** — Auditor General found serious weaknesses in the state response to intimate-partner violence, including uncertainty over reporting duties, poor coordination, and inconsistent municipal follow-up. [Riksrevisjonen lines 19–40](https://www.riksrevisjonen.no/rapporter-mappe/no-2021-2022/undersokelse-av-myndighetenes-innsats-mot-vold-i-nare-relasjoner/)
- **E042** — Police clearance rates for intimate-partner violence fell from 39% in 2015 to 24% in 2021; this is adverse institutional outcome evidence, not personal Støre evidence. [Riksrevisjonen lines 46–52, 93–102](https://www.riksrevisjonen.no/rapporter-mappe/no-2021-2022/undersokelse-av-myndighetenes-innsats-mot-vold-i-nare-relasjoner/)
- **E043** — U.S. State Department reported Sami women’s higher domestic/partner-violence exposure, limited Sami-language responders, and continuing barriers to reporting. [USDOS lines 189–197](https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2089707.html)
- **E044** — NGOs reported racial profiling of minority young men and increased online hate speech; authorities lacked disaggregated stop-and-search data. [USDOS lines 180–187](https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2089707.html)
- **E045** — Parliamentary Ombud found national data on minors held in police custody uncertain and announced follow-up with central authorities. [Sivilombudet lines 37–53](https://www.sivilombudet.no/en/besoksrapporter/new-visit-report-oslo-police-custody/)
- **E046** — Government follow-up records show that Fosen consultations and revised investigation programmes were active during 2022, while Sámi representatives considered the process too broad and potentially a relitigation of the Supreme Court judgment. [Government speech lines 314–321](https://www.regjeringen.no/no/aktuelt/l/id2966316/)

Shortfall: no direct Støre order, police-abuse finding, torture finding, or independent 2022 remedy outcome was recovered.

### 4B — institutions and rule of law

- **E047** — Supreme Court held that police intervention against an unannounced traffic-blocking protest did not breach freedom of assembly, while emphasizing that authorities must tolerate some disturbance. [Supreme Court lines 0–6](https://www.domstol.no/en/supremecourt/rulings/rulings-2022/supreme-court-criminal-cases/HR-2022-981-A/)
- **E048** — EOS Committee conducted parliamentary oversight of intelligence, surveillance, and security services, including inspections across NIS, PST, NSM, and defence bodies. [EOS report PDF pp. 6, 10–12](https://eos-utvalget.no/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/EOS-Committee-annual-report-2022.pdf)
- **E049** — EOS reported that NIS had failed to exercise due diligence in handling a source, while complaints concluded in 2022 produced no criticism of NIS. This is mixed oversight evidence. [EOS report PDF pp. 16–17](https://eos-utvalget.no/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/EOS-Committee-annual-report-2022.pdf)
- **E050** — EOS criticised PST for inadequate investigation and failure to provide documents during a complaint review, later receiving the relevant documents. [EOS report PDF pp. 19–20](https://eos-utvalget.no/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/EOS-Committee-annual-report-2022.pdf)
- **E051** — Data Protection Authority recorded 3,519 new cases in 2022, the highest number then recorded, showing active regulatory scrutiny but not censorship or executive retaliation. [Datatilsynet lines 502–503](https://www.datatilsynet.no/regelverk-og-verktoy/rapporter-og-utredninger/datatilsynets-arsrapporter/arsrapport-for-2022/?print=true)
- **E052** — The EOS framework explicitly exists to prevent rights violations and ensure intelligence services respect human rights, but classification rules limit public visibility into complaints and criticism. [EOS report PDF pp. 6, 11](https://eos-utvalget.no/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/EOS-Committee-annual-report-2022.pdf)

Shortfall: no evidence of Støre-directed censorship, opposition retaliation, unlawful surveillance, or term-limit manipulation was found.

### 5B — economic stewardship

- **E053** — Statistics Norway estimated average household net expenses rose NOK 18,000 in 2022, with somewhat higher burdens at the low end of the income distribution. [SSB lines 75–87](https://www.ssb.no/en/inntekt-og-forbruk/inntekt-og-formue/artikler/increased-expenditures-for-the-households--who-bears-the-largest-burden)
- **E054** — SSB found electricity subsidies reduced southern households’ costs but that vulnerable households devoted a larger budget share to electricity and had fewer substitution options. [SSB lines 78–101](https://www.ssb.no/en/energi-og-industri/energi/artikler/economic-consequences-of-high-electricity-prices-and-electricity-subsidy-scheme)
- **E055** — SSB found low-income households in apartment blocks reduced electricity use earlier but experienced welfare losses from constrained consumption. [SSB lines 94–101](https://www.ssb.no/en/energi-og-industri/energi/artikler/economic-consequences-of-high-electricity-prices-and-electricity-subsidy-scheme)
- **E056** — OECD identified falling labour-force participation, weak productivity growth, high housing costs, and future fiscal pressure as unresolved structural constraints. [OECD lines 3681–3689](https://www.oecd.org/en/about/news/press-releases/2022/02/norway-boosting-productivity-and-workforce-participation-while-improving-housing-affordability-will-help-maintain-high-living-standards.html)
- **E057** — Government electricity-support evaluation stated that universal support was administratively fair but that low-income households should receive more targeted assistance through housing benefits. [Government lines 195–201](https://www.regjeringen.no/no/aktuelt/okonomiske-konsekvenser-av-hoye-kraftpriser-og-stromstonad/id2927810/)
- **E058** — Consultation responses warned that proposed hourly electricity support would weaken saving incentives and favour higher-consumption households. [Government bill lines 295–305](https://www.regjeringen.no/no/dokumenter/prop.-116-l-20222023/id2976279/?ch=3)
- **E059** — SSB and other respondents warned that the design could reduce incentives for energy efficiency and weaken future energy-policy goals. [Government bill lines 298–303](https://www.regjeringen.no/no/dokumenter/prop.-116-l-20222023/id2976279/?ch=3)

Shortfall: no robust 2022 productivity outcome, competition investigation, procurement-attribution finding, or durable-growth evaluation was recovered.

### 6B — welfare and public services

- **E060** — SSB reported persistent low-income and material-deprivation burdens among single parents, disability-benefit recipients, immigrants, and low-income families with children. [SSB lines 75–92](https://www.ssb.no/en/inntekt-og-forbruk/inntekt-og-formue/artikler/the-economic-welfare-of-low-income-households-2022)
- **E061** — Helsetilsynet found 49 of 70 NAV offices open six hours or less per week, with delays particularly affecting users unable to use digital channels. [Helsetilsynet lines 169–182](https://www.helsetilsynet.no/publikasjoner/arsrapporter/arsrapport-helsetilsynet-2022/3.-arets-aktiviteter-og-resultater?b=toc_749319)
- **E062** — Helsetilsynet reported 153,000 people lacked a regular general practitioner in Q1 2022, with risks concentrated among older and medically complex patients. [Helsetilsynet lines 183–189](https://www.helsetilsynet.no/publikasjoner/arsrapporter/arsrapport-helsetilsynet-2022/3.-arets-aktiviteter-og-resultater?b=toc_749319)
- **E063** — Specialist-healthcare waiting time rose to 66 days in 2022, five days above 2021, with particularly high concern around mental-health services. [Government lines 178–193](https://www.regjeringen.no/no/aktuelt/okte-ventetider-i-spesialisthelsetjenesten-i-2022/id2966979/)
- **E064** — Government follow-up of Fosen documented continuing consultations, updated investigations, and unresolved Sámi-rights implementation during the target period. [Government lines 205–225](https://www.regjeringen.no/no/aktuelt/l/id2966316/)
- **E065** — Independent refugee interviews found generally positive reception by police, NAV, UDI, and municipalities, but uneven access to medicines and other services. [IMDi/NIBR lines 36–54](https://arkiv.imdi.no/arkiv/arkiverte-publikasjoner/rapport-om-ukrainske-flyktningers-mote-med-norge/)
- **E066** — Refugee interviews recommended more coordinated information-sharing, more equal services across municipalities, and better information flow. [IMDi/NIBR lines 83–85](https://arkiv.imdi.no/arkiv/arkiverte-publikasjoner/rapport-om-ukrainske-flyktningers-mote-med-norge/)

Shortfall: no comprehensive regional welfare evaluation, child-poverty causal estimate, or durable programme-outcome study was recovered.

### 7B — personal integrity

- **E067** — Supreme Court clarified that corruption requires a sufficiently strong connection between an improper benefit and the recipient’s public position; the ruling concerned a municipal official, not Støre. [Supreme Court lines 0–6](https://www.domstol.no/no/hoyesterett/avgjorelser/2022/hoyesterett---straff/HR-2022-1278-A/)
- **E068** — Foreign Service Control Unit recorded 121 new financial-irregularity cases in 2022; 44 required a response, including four corruption cases. These concern grant administration, not personal Støre conduct. [MFA report lines 199–200, 264–268](https://www.regjeringen.no/en/documents/report-on-cases-of-financial-irregularities-in-2022/id2971508/)
- **E069** — The same report states that detected cases are not necessarily representative because some irregularities are easier to uncover than others. This is a contrary closed-system limitation. [MFA report lines 264–268](https://www.regjeringen.no/en/documents/report-on-cases-of-financial-irregularities-in-2022/id2971508/)
- **E070** — Norwegian anti-corruption procedures allowed anonymous or open reporting, suspension of disbursements, external experts, forensic audits, repayment, and possible police referral. [MFA report lines 181–189](https://www.regjeringen.no/en/documents/report-on-cases-of-financial-irregularities-in-2022/id2971508/)
- **E071** — GRECO found regular ethics training for the incoming government was not demonstrated, and several disclosure, review, lobbying, and sanction recommendations remained unimplemented. [GRECO PDF pp. 2, 6–7](https://rm.coe.int/fifth-evaluation-round-preventing-corruption-and-promoting-integrity-i/1680a9b330)
- **E072** — GRECO found the conflict-of-interest procedure partly implemented: self-assessment and legal advice existed, but concrete revolving-door guidance remained incomplete. [GRECO PDF pp. 4–6](https://rm.coe.int/fifth-evaluation-round-preventing-corruption-and-promoting-integrity-i/1680a9b330)

Shortfall: no source established Støre’s personal benefit, direction, protection, obstruction, procurement favoritism, or corrupt financial conduct.

### 8B — effectiveness and implementation

- **E073** — Independent refugee interviews found high satisfaction with initial reception but unequal access to some services, providing positive implementation evidence with subgroup limitations. [IMDi/NIBR lines 47–54](https://arkiv.imdi.no/arkiv/arkiverte-publikasjoner/rapport-om-ukrainske-flyktningers-mote-med-norge/)
- **E074** — Public-health research found Ukrainian refugees arriving in 2022 had poorer self-rated health, more psychological distress, and unmet healthcare needs, especially among newer arrivals. [NIPH lines 18–25, 51–63](https://www.fhi.no/en/publ/2023/Healthcare-needs-among-refugees-from-ukraine-arriving-in-norway-during-2022/)
- **E075** — Eurofound later found that refugee integration measures still faced unstable housing, childcare capacity, mental-health access, unstable employment, and fragmented support. [Eurofound lines 39–45, 60–75](https://www.eurofound.europa.eu/en/publications/all/social-impact-migration-addressing-challenges-receiving-and-integrating-ukrainian)
- **E076** — Norway’s December 2022 cyber-resilience white paper formally identified national-control and coordination measures, but the associated implementation record remained policy-level. [Government white-paper record lines 152–167](https://www.regjeringen.no/en/documents/meld.-st.-9-20222023/id2950130/)
- **E077** — NSM reported increased compromise attempts against Norwegian organisations in the first half of 2022 and identified technology, research, public administration, energy, and communications as exposed sectors. [NSM lines 256–269](https://nsm.no/aktuelt/digitalt-risikobilde-2022-cyberangrep-har-blitt-hverdagskost)
- **E078** — NSM specifically stated that many incidents could have been avoided through basic security measures, providing adverse implementation evidence against any claim of complete cyber effectiveness. [NSM lines 259–265](https://nsm.no/aktuelt/digitalt-risikobilde-2022-cyberangrep-har-blitt-hverdagskost)
- **E079** — Helsetilsynet documented service-access failures and subsequent NAV improvement work, showing both adverse outcomes and partial institutional response. [Helsetilsynet lines 174–182](https://www.helsetilsynet.no/publikasjoner/arsrapporter/arsrapport-helsetilsynet-2022/3.-arets-aktiviteter-og-resultater?b=toc_749319)

Shortfall: durable outcomes, causal attribution to Støre personally, and independent recipient-side assessment of Ukraine and cyber policy remain unresolved.

All units above are evidence or explicitly limited contrary/context claims; none assigns a score, range, ranking, or scoring advice.
